site: Murray Buttes, Gale crater. Quela drill site at the foot of Murray Butte 12

terrain.projection: Equirectangular, sphere radius 3396190 m, centre longitude 0, standard parallel 0

parkingSpot.description: Curiosity's position at the end of the sol 1455 drive. It stayed here until the sol 1468 drive, which covers the radiation paper's butte period (sols 1456 to 1467)

nearCrop.description: 3 km square at full resolution, centred on the parking spot. Exact pixel window, so no resampling
nearCrop.note: parkingSpotInCrop is in GDAL pixel coordinates, where whole numbers are cell corners. Code should use parkingSpotLocal (local metres, see shared/conventions.md)

farCrop.description: Whole mosaic at 20 m per pixel, for the distant horizon
farCrop.command: gdal_translate -tr 20 20 -r average -of ENVI -ot Float32 MSL_Gale_DEM_Mosaic_1m_v3.tif far.bin

paperTarget.source: Ehresmann et al. 2021, Natural Radiation Shielding on Mars Measured With the MSL/RAD Instrument, JGR Planets

referenceCheck.description: Values from a quick independent script, for testing the engine against. Not from the paper
referenceCheck.method: Observer 1 m above the terrain. 360 azimuths. Marched in 0.5 m steps out to 280 m with bilinear sampling. Local terrain only, no distant horizon and no curvature. Blocked fraction is the mean of sin(skyline elevation), negative elevations counted as 0. Positions are in local metres and cell centres are at half-pixel offsets
referenceCheck.note: An earlier version gave blockedAtParkingSpot 0.149. That run sampled with a half-pixel offset (whole-number pixel coordinates treated as cell centres)
referenceCheck.blockedWithin5mTowardsButte: 0.19 to 0.21 (5 m north and north-west of the spot)
referenceCheck.butteTopAboveSpot: about 8 to 9 m, 10 to 20 m to the north and north-west

sky.source: JPL Horizons, airless apparent, site 137.353006 E, -4.695202

base.doseFactorNote: Assumption: the base is a normal shielded habitat; its dose rate is this fraction of open ground
base.note: Candidate C from engine base-candidates: the highest base-link coverage of the three southern candidates (0.504 of layer cells, against 0.455 at Curiosity's sol 1480 position and 0.383 at sol 1471). The previous base at Curiosity's sol 1439 position (1506.1, 1678.3), among the buttes, linked only 0.084. Chosen for line of sight, not a rover position

plannerBounds.note: Local metres. A mosaic seam runs roughly north-south at local x 1580 to 1605, inside these bounds; its step is about 0.5 m north of y 1600 and under 0.15 m further south, too small to affect planning. The east limit excludes a separate doubtful band near x 1700

notes.walkSpeed: Assumption: suited walking speed on flat ground, metres per second. Walking time per metre is (1 / walkSpeed) * (1 + (slope / 15)^2)
notes.maxSlopeDeg: Assumption: ground steeper than this, in degrees, is impassable
notes.shelterBlockedMin: Assumption: a shelter cell has at least this blocked-sky fraction
notes.shelterMaxSlopeDeg: Assumption: a shelter cell is no steeper than this, in degrees
notes.minutesToShelterLimit: Assumption: more minutes than this to the nearest refuge counts as a warning (the relay's warning limit and a route penalty)
notes.waypointSpacing: Assumption: metres between waypoints; every stop is always a waypoint
notes.openBlocked: Assumption: blocked-sky fraction of open ground, where the relative dose rate is 1
notes.doseShieldingFactor: Assumption: relative dose rate = 1 - doseShieldingFactor * (blocked - openBlocked), kept between 0.5 and 1.05. Calibrated to Curiosity's measurement that about 9 more points of blocked sky cut the dose by about 5 percent. Simulated, not a dose model
notes.oxygenMinutes: Assumption: minutes of oxygen at the start; oxygenFraction = 1 - minutes elapsed / oxygenMinutes
notes.doseBudget: Simulated: doseFraction is accumulated rate * minutes divided by a budget of twice the planned main-route duration at rate 1, clamped to 0..1

notes.leadMinutes: Assumption: minutes of warning between the storm being declared and the storm arriving
notes.stormMinutes: Assumption: how long the storm lasts once it arrives, in minutes
notes.doseMultiplier: Assumption: dose rate during the storm relative to normal, applied to walking and sheltering once it arrives (and to reroute dose)
notes.noLinkPenalty: Assumption: a site without a base link scores this fraction worse (0.05 = 5 percent)
notes.maxMinutesToCover: Hard rule. The astronaut must be under cover within this many minutes of the warning, so they are not walking in the open when the storm arrives. Normally equal to leadMinutes

notes: The waypoint file's easting and northing are already in the terrain mosaic's projection. No conversion needed.
The terrain at the waypoint reads -4379.53 m against the waypoint's own -4379.46 m, so the route and the terrain line up with no offset.
There is a visible seam in the mosaic running roughly north to south about 80 m east of the route. Treat steep cells along it as an artefact.
Sun and Earth directions and the date for the demo are still to be added.
